newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia raises bank capital adequacy ratios.
newsitem.headline: Estonia raises bank capital adequacy ratios.

text.p: Estonia's central bank on Wednesday said that it is to raise the capital adequacy ratios of commercial banks.
Officials have expressed concern over the rapid pace of bank lending in Estonia, which grew by 70 percent in 1996 compared with expected economic growth of around four to five percent.
The central bank said capital adequacy ratios would rise on October 1 from eight to 10 percent and it would also change the way that the ratios were calculated.
"Although the main target is to decrease structural differences, they will also have a tightening effect on banks' expansion plans," the central bank said.
"The Bank of Estonia sees the requirements to secure the banking sector in the context of the goverment's plans to strengthen overall fiscal discipline," it added.
The raising of capital adequacy ratios is part of Estonia's latest agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for standby credits.
Estonia has also introduced laws to tighten rules for local government borrowing as it must cut the public sector deficit from 1.5 percent of GDP in 1996 to 0.5 percent this year.
The central government budget is balanced.
IMF Estonia and Latvia resident representative Dimitri Demekas welcomed the rise in capital adequacy ratios.
"We are happy and this (a rise in the ratios) is part of the programme that we agreed with Estonia," Demekas said.
"It may have an small curbing effect on the rate of growth of credit but at the same time it will boost confidence in the Estonian banking system," Demekas added.
"I do not expect a dampening of economic growth," he added.
